These CORE requirements have no task covering them yet (a task covers a requirement by listing its id in requirement_ids):
- R-016: Marking a handoff complete produces exactly one immutable audit/receipt object with an internal view and a privacy-filtered shareable projection (no child name/address).
- R-017: Every outcome-affecting action carries a client-generated idempotent action ID; the server handles duplicates idempotently.
- R-018: A force-quit mid-accept (after tap, before ack) followed by relaunch reconciles from server truth with no duplicate writes and no false local state.
- R-019: Same-day cutoffs and elapsed/aging calculations are computed server-side in UTC plus a pod home timezone set at pod creation — no client-local-time logic.
- R-020: The pod creator can revoke and reissue the join code; the old code is invalidated immediately.
- R-021: The audit/receipt record persists after either party deletes their account, rendering the departed party as a placeholder.
- R-022: UI copy explicitly states 'accepted' means a trusted member claimed responsibility, never that arrival/help is guaranteed.
- R-023: A brand-new pod with no other members shows a distinct empty state/CTA ('share the invite'), separate from 'pod has members but nobody has responded' (re-broadcast/escalate CTA).
- R-024: Both the post funnel and the accept/resolve/complete funnel implement and can demonstrate all four states: loading, empty, error, success.
- R-025: No GPS/live location, ETA, or map features anywhere in the app.
- R-026: No in-app chat/DM thread; only the request card plus one optional short note.
- R-027: No payments, tipping, or monetary fields anywhere in the app.
- R-028: No recurring or future-scheduled requests — every request is same-day only.
- R-029: No persistent scrollable request-history/feed screen beyond individual per-request receipts.
- R-030: No pod-admin console or member-management UI beyond create-pod-get-code and the one revoke/reissue capability.

Re-emit a SINGLE corrected ```tasks-json``` fenced block — the whole backlog, not a diff — that adds or updates tasks (via requirement_ids) so every one of these is covered by at least one task.
